diagnostic_evidence.quote: Any bounded sequence in Barron space $\mathcal{B}_1$ has a subsequence that converges in $H^1(\Omega)$
there exists a constant $C(\Omega,d)$ such that for all $f\in \mathcal{B}_1$ there holds $\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,d)\|f\|_{\mathcal{B}_1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: A continuous embedding B_1 -> H^1 only yields H^1-boundedness of a B_1-bounded sequence, not a convergent subsequence in H^1. The first assertion of the lemma (H^1-compactness) is exactly what the theorems on H^1 convergence need, and the cited fact does not establish it; a genuinely different argument (e.g. BV/L^infty bounds on gradients of Barron functions plus Arzela-Ascoli) is required.

failure_location.quote: It follows from the fact that $\mathcal{B}_1$ is continuously embedded into $H^1(\Omega)$, and $H^1(\Omega)$ is compactly embedded into $L^2(\Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and prove (or cite) a lemma that the embedding B_1 -> H^1(Omega) is compact for bounded Lipschitz Omega (gradients of Barron functions are bounded in L^infty and BV, so bounded sets are relatively compact in L^2), then invoke it in Theorems main and main2.
issues.overall_effect: The H^1 convergence claims of Theorem main and of Theorem main2 (case R_2) rest on an unproved compactness statement; only L^2 convergence is supported by the given proof.
issues.title: Compactness of B_1-bounded sequences in H^1 deduced from mere continuous embedding
issues.why_classification: The statement appears true, but its justification is invalid and the repair needs a new nontrivial lemma; the H^1 conclusions of two main theorems depend on it.

issues.failure_explanation: A monotone increasing r(n) need not diverge (e.g. any bounded r as in Theorem main). If sup r(n) < c_rho(f^dagger), no class X_{n,r(n)} contains the approximants used in the proof and the discrepancy need never drop below tau*delta, so finite termination fails. The proof's use of r^{-1}(c_rho(f^dagger)) and 'r(n) -> +infty' is an unstated hypothesis, contradicting the prose that no conditions on r(n) are needed.

failure_location.quote: On the other hand, by the definition of $r(n)$, we have $r(n)\to +\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis r(n) -> +infty (or lim r(n) > c_rho(f^dagger)) to Theorem main2 and remove the 'without requiring additional conditions on r(n)' statement.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem main2 as stated is false for bounded radius maps; the claim that Algorithm 2 needs no condition on r(n) is incorrect.
issues.title: Theorem main2 proof assumes r(n) -> infinity, not stated in hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A one-line standard hypothesis restores the proof; method, rates and the 'no knowledge of c_rho' scope survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The VSC is local, so (errorestimate) requires ||f^delta_{n,alpha}-f^dagger||_{L^2} < epsilon. Statement (i) asserts the bound for arbitrary small alpha, delta with no coupling to n and no uniqueness, which the argument does not support; e.g. alpha << delta admits minimizers far from f^dagger. Also alpha(delta) ~ delta/Phi(tau delta) need not tend to 0 (Phi Lipschitz at 0), violating (choicealpha).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for the inverse function $\Phi^{-1}$ and its conjugate $\Phi^{-*}$

issues.failure_explanation: For a concave index function (e.g. Phi(t)=c_0 t^mu), alpha t - Phi(t) -> +infty as t -> infty, so Phi^*(alpha) = +infty for every alpha > 0 and its inverse is meaningless; the term tau^{-1}Phi^{-*}(tau alpha) in (errorestimate) is undefined as stated. The proof instead uses the Fenchel conjugate of the convex inverse Phi^{-1}, which is the object actually needed in the Young inequality.

failure_location.quote: $\Phi^{-*}$ denotes the (generalized) inverse of the Fenchel conjugate $\Phi^*$ of $\Phi$, defined by $\Phi^*(\alpha) := \sup_{t \ge 0} \{\alpha t - \Phi(t)\}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Phi^{-*} := (Phi^{-1})^*, the Fenchel conjugate of the convex inverse function, in the theorem statement.
issues.overall_effect: The error estimate (errorestimate) in the theorem statement involves an ill-defined quantity; the intended bound is recoverable from the proof.
issues.title: Phi^{-*} defined via Fenchel conjugate of concave Phi, which is identically +infty
issues.why_classification: Local redefinition; the proof already uses the correct object and the rate is unaffected.
